parts.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write a short essay on the challenges of living in a big city. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.

reference.commentary:
【1】引出话题:大城市数量不断增加。
【2】指出问题:在大城市生活有诸多挑战。
【3】【4】【6】使用The first problem、Next和Another consequence分别引出对三个挑战的具体阐述(不一定拘泥于“第一”“第二”“第三”的表述)。
【5】运用so...that...句型和unless引导的条件状语,增加句式多样性。
【7】以交际方式结尾,增强互动性。
reference.modelEssay: The Challenges of Living in a Big City With the development of economy and urbanization, the number of big cities is constantly increasing in China.While big cities are attracting more and more people, they also bring many challenges, such as traffic jams and pollution, just to name a few.The first problem that really bothers me is the traffic congestion in the rush hour. I hate waiting for buses and being late. Therefore, I have to get up very early if I have an appointment in the morning.Next is that the large population in a big city makes itso crowded that you can't find a peaceful place unless staying at home. The supermarkets are always crowded, so are the cinemas and parks.Another consequence of such a large population is that it intensifies the inadequacy of quality medical and educational resources, thus decreasing residents' sense of happiness.As a result, although I am frequently asked whether I like to live in a big city or not, my answer is always no, definitely not. How about you?
reference.shenTi: 本题要求就大城市生活的挑战发表看法。写作时可从交通拥堵、人口拥挤、优质医疗与教育资源不足等方面展开，最后表明自己的态度。

banked_cloze.fullTextTranslation:
每年都有数百万人因为空气污染而早早死去。就福利成本而言，空气污染每年造成多于5万亿美元的全球经济损失，而对发展中国家的损害是最为严重的。
该数据包含了一些与空气污染相关的费用。仅每年的收入损失就达到2,250亿美元。
报告涵盖了户内和户外的空气污染。户内空气污染源于诸如家用取暖和家用烹饪等。在过去几十年中，虽然这方面有所改善，但户内空气污染仍然持续不断。户外空气污染的程度则随着工业和交通的快速发展而迅速加剧。
健康指标与评估研究所所长克里斯·穆瑞将这份报告描述为一项“呼吁采取行动的紧急号召”。他说：“导致人们过早死亡的一个风险因素就是我们吸入的空气，而这是我们个人几乎无法控制的一个因素。”
空气污染产生的影响在发展中国家最为严重，在发展中国家的一些地区，劳动力损失所带来的收入损失相当于几乎1%的国内生产总值。在中低收入国家，大概有十分之九的人们在居住地经常遭受着危险的户外空气污染。
但这一问题并不仅仅局限在发展中国家。在美国，成千上万的人们因为相关疾病而过早死去。近年来，在许多欧洲国家，随着柴油车辆日益普遍，因为相关疾病而过早死去的人的数量达到了几万人。
banked_cloze.overview:
本文主要讲述空气污染对全球经济和人类生命的损害问题。
第1、2段提出论点：空气污染缩短人类寿命并造成巨大的全球经济损失。
第3段指出导致空气污染的原因。
第4—6段阐述治理空气污染的紧迫性，并指出空气污染不仅给发展中国家造成巨大损害，也严重影响发达国家。

加利福尼亚多年来一直面临着干旱问题，一些地方甚至不得不从数百英里以外的地方抽运淡水到其配水系统。随着该州人口的不断增长，这一问题正在加剧。（46）新的研究发现，该州地下有深层地下水储备，这可以帮助他们解决干旱危机。以前的钻井深度只能达到地下1,000英尺，但是由于新的抽水实践的进行，现在能抽取出比这更深的地下水。斯坦福大学的研究小组对1,000英尺以下的地下蓄水层进行了勘测，并发现其蓄水量或许是先前认为的三倍。
(47) 从1,000英尺以下的深度开采石油和天然气是有利可图的，但在加利福尼亚，从1,000英尺以下抽取地下水只是最近才变得有利可图。地下蓄水层在地下1,000英尺到3,000英尺之间，这意味着抽水成本是昂贵的，而且还有一些其他的担忧。(48)从这一深度取水最大的担忧就是陆地表面会逐渐下陷。随着地下水被抽走，地下留出的空余空间会被上面的土壤压实。
尽管从这样的深度取水的成本很高，但这仍比在这个大部分地区都沿海的州淡化海水的成本低。在条件可行的地方，有一些淡化海水的工厂，但它们的运营成本很高，而且可能需要不断的维修。（49）地下井是更为可靠的淡水来源，加利福尼亚正期望这些深井可以解决他们严重的淡水短缺问题。
(50) 这些水源的一个问题就是深层地下水比浅一些的地下水的含盐浓度要高。这就意味着从一些井里抽取上来的水可能需要进行淡化，因而会增加成本。根据950多个钻井日志而进行的地下水详细研究刚刚被发表。据最新估计，目前地下淡水储存量达到27,000亿立方米。

人工智能的一个例子就是无人驾驶汽车。它们已经行驶在加利福尼亚的公路上了，所以现在问我们是否能给机器编入程序，使之能合乎伦理地做事情也不算太早了。随着无人驾驶汽车的改进，它们将可以拯救生命。它们将比人类司机犯的错误更少。（52）然而，它们有的时候会面临生命之间的抉择。是不是要给这些汽车编入避免碰撞过路儿童的程序，即使那样会使车上的乘客陷入危险中？或是为了躲避一只狗而急转弯？如果这样做的风险仅仅是会造成车辆的损伤，而不会危及乘客呢？

几乎在阿尔法围棋取胜的同时，微软的“聊天机器人”的表现却不尽如人意。该软件名叫泰勒，旨在回答那些18到24岁的人们发出的信息。泰勒应该能够从她所接收的信息中学习。(54)她被设计得可以慢慢提高其处理对话的能力，但是有些人在教她一些种族主义的观点。当她开始说希特勒好话的时候，微软公司将她关闭，并删除了她最恶劣的言论。

26. 【考点】名词辨析题。
F) 【语法判断】空格前面是形容词最高级 the most serious,后面为现在分词结构 occurring in the developing world 作后置定语,因此空格处需要填入名词。
【语义判断】本句前半部分提到，就福利成本而言，空气污染每年造成多于5万亿美元的全球经济损失。由此可知，后半部分应指，对于发展中国家而言，空气污染会造成最为严重的影响。因此，空格处需要填入一个表示“不良影响”或“损失”的名词。由此确定名词damage“损害”为本题答案。

27. 【考点】固定用法题。
B) 【语法判断】空格前面为名词词组 a number of costs,后面为介宾结构 with air pollution。通过分析句子结构可知，空格处所填词应与后面的介宾结构一起作前面名词词组的后置定语。因此，空格处需要填入形容词或动词的分词形式。
【语义判断】文章首段提到，空气污染每年造成多于5万亿美元的全球经济损失。本句承接首段指出，该数据包含了一些费用。因此，空格处所填词应与后面的with air pollution搭配，共同表达“与空气污染相关”的意思。备选词中符合以上要求的只有associated。be associated with...意为“与……相关”，由此确定associated为答案。本句完整形式为“The figures include a number of costs which are associated with air pollution.”，原文中省略了which are。

28. 【考点】名词辨析题。
M) 【语法判断】空格前面为动词 includes，后面有介词 like 表示列举，因此空格处需要填入名词来作宾语。
【语义判断】文章围绕 air pollution 展开，本句中提到 Indoor pollution，并列举了两种户内空气污染的情况是“家用取暖和家用烹饪”，因此空格处所填名词意思上与家用取暖和家用烹饪有关。根
据生活常识可知，取暖与烹饪均会产生一定的空气污染。因此，空格处需要填入一个表示“原因，根源”的名词。由此确定名词 sources“根源”为本题答案。

29. 【考点】形容词辨析题。
D) 【语法判断】空格前为系动词 remained，后为介词短语，因此空格处应填入形容词作表语。
【语义判断】本句末尾处使用介词 despite，表示让步，表达了“虽然家用取暖和家用烹饪这方面有所改善”这一语义。因此，本句前面部分在意思上应该与末尾的介宾结构相反，所以空格处需要填入一个与 remained 一起表示户内空气污染“依旧存在”的形容词。由此确定形容词 constant“持续不断的”为本题答案。

30. 【考点】动词辨析题。
G) 【语法判断】空格前面为人名 Chris Murray, 空格后面为代词 it, 因此判断空格处所填词为动词, 且该动词能与宾语 it 后面的介词 as 搭配, an “urgent call to action” 则为 it 的宾语补足语。
【语义判断】本句指出，这份报告是一项“呼吁采取行动的紧急号召”。备选动词中，described 意为“形容，描述”，可与 as 搭配，符合句意，故为答案。described...as...意为“将……描述为……”。

31. 【考点】名词辨析题。
E) 【语法判断】空格前有动词 have 和限定词 little，所以空格处需要填入名词。
【语义判断】本句指出，导致人们过早死亡的一个风险因素就是我们吸入的空气。由常识可知，空气是人类生存所必需的客观条件，人们几乎无法操控。因此，空格处应填入一个表示“操控”的名词，故 E）control“控制”为本题的答案。

32. 【考点】动词辨析题。
H) 【语法判断】通过分析句子结构可知，空格位于where引导的定语从句中，空格前为名词词组lost-labor income作主语，空格后为副词nearly和名词结构1% of GDP，所以该从句缺少谓语动词，再根据本句前半部分的时态，空格处应填入动词的第三人称单数形式。
【语义判断】本句前半部分指出，空气污染产生的影响在发展中国家最为严重。空格所在从句进一步说明严重的程度。又因为从句的主语和宾语均为经济学名词结构，因此空格处填入 equals“相当于”符合句意，意为“劳动力损失所带来的收入损失相当于几乎1%的国内生产总值”，表明空气污染产生的影响之严重。

33. 【考点】副词辨析题。
K) 【语法判断】空格前面是代词 they，后面为动词 experience，因此空格处需要填入副词以修饰其后的动词。
【语义判断】前一句提到，在发展中国家的一些地区，劳动力损失所带来的收入损失相当于几乎1%的国内生产总值。空格所在句进一步解释造成劳动力损失的原因：在中低收入国家，大概有十分之九的人们在居住的地方经受着危险的户外空气污染。因此，空格处需要填入一个表示“长期以来，一直这样”的副词，修饰 experience。由此确定副词 regularly“经常”为本题答案。

34. 【考点】副词辨析题。
I) 【语法判断】空格位于 be limited to 这个固定用法中，且本句基本结构完整，因此空格处需要填入副词修饰 limited。
【语义判断】前一段提到了空气污染给发展中国家带来的影响。空格所在句之后则阐述了空气污染对发达国家的影响。因此，空格处需要填入一个与 is not limited to 一起表示“不仅仅局限于”的副词，表明这一情况并非只发生在发展中国家。由此确定副词 exclusively“仅仅，唯独”为本题答案。

35. 【考点】名词辨析题。
O) 【语法判断】空格前为名词 diesel，空格后为谓语动词 have become more common，所以空格处需要填入名词的复数形式，与名词 diesel 搭配构成从句的主语。
【语义判断】通过上下文可知，本段的大意是空气污染对发达国家也产生了很大影响；近年来，欧洲国家柴油车辆的日益普遍使得欧洲发达国家也面临着严重的空气污染，导致因相关疾病而过早死去的人的数量达到了几万人。因此，可以确定名词 vehicles“交通工具，车辆”为本题答案。

paragraphs.text: Several times a month, you can find a doctor in the aisles of Ralph's market in Huntington Beach, California, wearing a white coat and helping people learn about food. On one recent day, this doctor was Daniel Nadeau, wandering the cereal aisle with Allison Scott, giving her some idea on how to feed kids who persistently avoid anything that is healthy. "Have you thought about trying fresh juices in the morning?" he asks her. "The frozen oranges and apples are a little cheaper, and fruits are really good for the brain. Juices are quick and easy to prepare, you can take the frozen fruit out the night before and have it ready the next morning."

Scott is delighted to get food advice from a physician who is program director of the nearby Mary and Dick Allen Diabetes Center, part of the St. Joseph Hoag Health alliance. The center's ‘Shop with Your Doc' program sends doctors to the grocery store to meet with any patients who sign up for the service, plus any other shoppers who happen to be around with questions.

Nadeau notices the pre-made macaroni (通心粉)-and-cheese boxes in Scott's shopping cart and suggests she switch to whole grain macaroni and real cheese. "So I'd have to make it?"she asks, her enthusiasm fading at the thought of how long that might take, just to have her kids reject it. "I'm not sure they'd eat it. They just won't eat it."

Nadeau says sugar and processed foods are big contributors to the rising diabetes rates among children. "In America, over 50 percent of our food is processed food," Nadeau tells her. "And only 5 percent of our food is plant-based food. I think we should try to reverse that." Scott agrees to try more fruit juices for the kids and to make real macaroni and cheese. Score one point for the doctor, zero for diabetes.

Nadeau is part of a small revolution developing across California. The food-as-medicine movement has been around for decades, but it's making progress as physicians and medical institutions make food a formal part of treatment, rather than relying solely on medications (药物). By prescribing nutritional changes or launching programs such as ‘Shop with your Doc', they are trying to prevent, limit or even reverse disease by changing what patients eat. "There's no question people can take things a long way toward reversing diabetes, reversing high blood pressure, even preventing cancer by food choices," Nadeau says.

In the big picture, says Dr. Richard Afable, CEO and president of ST. Joseph Hoag Health, medical institutions across the state are starting to make a philosophical switch to becoming a health organization, not just a health care organization. That feeling echoes the beliefs of the Therapeutic Food Pantry program at Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital, which completed its pilot phase and is about to expand on an ongoing basis to five clinic sites throughout the city. The program will offer patients several bags of food prescribed for their condition, along with intensive training in how to cook it. "We really want to link food and medicine, and not just give away food," says Dr. Rita Nguyen, the hospital's medical director of Healthy Food Initiatives. "We want people to understand what they're eating, how to prepare it, the role food plays in their lives."

In Southern California, Loma Linda University School of Medicine is offering specialized training for its resident physicians in Lifestyle Medicine — that is a formal specialty in using food to treat disease. Research findings increasingly show the power of food to treat or reverse diseases, but that does not mean that diet alone is always the solution, or that every illness can benefit substantially from dietary changes. Nonetheless, physicians say that they look at the collective data and a clear picture emerges: that the salt, sugar, fat and processed foods in the American diet contribute to the nation's high rates of obesity, diabetes and heart disease. According to the World Health Organization, 80 percent of deaths from heart disease and stroke are caused by high blood pressure, tobacco use, elevated cholesterol and low consumption of fruits and vegetables.

"It's a different paradigm(范式) of how to treat disease," says Dr. Brenda Rea, who helps run the family and preventive medicine residency program at Loma Linda University School of Medicine. The lifestyle medicine specialty is designed to train doctors in how to prevent and treat disease, in part, by changing patients' nutritional habits. The medical center and school at Loma Linda also has a food cupboard and kitchen for patients. This way, patients not only learn about which foods to buy, but also how to prepare them at home.

Many people don't know how to cook, Rea says, and they only know how to heat things up. That means depending on packaged food with high salt and sugar content. So teaching people about which foods are healthy and how to prepare them, she says, can actually transform a patient's life. And beyond that, it might transform the health and lives of that patient's family. "What people eat can be medicine or poison," Rea says. "As a physician, nutrition is one of the most powerful things you can change to reverse the effects of long-term disease."

Studies have explored evidence that dietary changes can slow inflammation(炎症), for example, or make the body inhospitable to cancer cells. In general, many lifestyle medicine physicians recommend a plant-based diet — particularly for people with diabetes or other inflammatory conditions.

"As what happened with tobacco, this will require a cultural shift, but that can happen," says Nguyen. "In the same way physicians used to smoke, and then stopped smoking and were able to talk to patients about it, I think physicians can have a bigger voice in it."

blocks.text: California has been facing a drought for many years now, with certain areas even having to pump freshwater hundreds of miles to their distribution system. The problem is growing as the population of the state continues to expand. New research has found deep water reserves under the state which could help solve their drought crisis. Previous drilling of wells could only reach depths of 1,000 feet, but due to new pumping practices, water deeper than this can now be extracted (抽取). The team at Stanford investigated the aquifers(地下蓄水层)below this depth and found that reserves may be triple what was previously thought.

It is profitable to drill to depths more than 1,000 feet for oil and gas extraction, but only recently in California has it become profitable to pump water from this depth. The aquifers range from 1,000 to 3,000 feet below the ground, which means that pumping will be expensive and there are other concerns. The biggest concern of pumping out water from this deep in the gradual settling down of the land surface. As the water is pumped out, the vacant space left is compacted by the weight of the earth above.

Even though pumping from these depths is expensive, it is still cheaper than desalinating(脱盐)the ocean water in the largely coastal state. Some desalination plants exist where feasible, but they are costly to run and can need constant repairs. Wells are much more reliable sources of freshwater, and California is hoping that these deep wells may be the answer to their severe water shortage.

One problem with these sources is that the deep water also has a higher level of salt than shallower aquifers. This means that some wells may even need to undergo desalination after extraction, thus increasing the cost. Research from the exhaustive study of groundwater from over 950 drilling logs has just been published. New estimates of the water reserves now go up to 2,700 billion cubic meters of freshwater.

items.stemEn: What does Eric Schmidt think of artificial intelligence?

blocks.text: The AlphaGo program's victory is an example of how smart computers have become. But can artificial intelligence (AI) machines act ethically, meaning can they be honest and fair? One example of AI is driverless cars. They are already on California roads, so it is not too soon to ask whether we can program a machine to act ethically. As driverless cars improve, they will save lives. They will make fewer mistakes than human drivers do. Sometimes, however, they will face a choice between lives. Should the cars be programmed to avoid hitting a child running across the road, even if that will put their passengers at risk? What about making a sudden turn to avoid a dog? What if the only risk is damage to the car itself, not to the passengers? Perhaps there will be lessons to learn from driverless cars, but they are not super-intelligent beings. Teaching ethics to a machine even more intelligent than we are will be the bigger challenge.

About the same time as AlphaGo's triumph, Microsoft's ‘chatbot' took a bad turn. The software, named Taylor, was designed to answer messages from people aged 18-24. Taylor was supposed to be able to learn from the messages she received. She was designed to slowly improve her ability to handle conversations, but some people were teaching Taylor racist ideas. When she started saying nice things about Hitler, Microsoft turned her off and deleted her ugliest messages. AlphaGo's victory and Taylor's defeat happened at about the same time. This should be a warning to us. It is one thing to use AI within a game with clear rules and clear goals. It is something very different to use AI in the real world. The unpredictability of the real world may bring to the surface a troubling software problem.

Eric Schmidt is one of the bosses of Google, which own AlphoGo. He thinks AI will be positive for humans. He said people will be the winner, whatever the outcome. Advances in AI will make human beings smarter, more able and "just better human beings."

reference.commentary:
1. 翻译第一句时，注意“以惊人速度增长”有多种表达方式，可译为 has increased at a(n) phenomenal/remarkable/astonishing rate，也可译为 has grown with surprising rapidity。
2. 第二句较短，且与第一句逻辑关系紧密，可处理为 which 引导的非限制性定语从句，与第一句合译为一句。句中的“极大地改变了”可以直接译为 has greatly/enormously changed，也可以像参考译文一样将其译为 has made major changes to。

5. 翻译最后一句时，“稳步增长”可用 is growing steadily 来表达，也可将其转化为名词形式，翻译为 the steady growth。
